subject: Aurora stability debrief - playbook & ownership ladder
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@aurora.com>, Aurora SRE Team <ops@aurora.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora stability debrief - initial RCA and next steps

Hi Jenna / Aurora ops,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Attached is the formal RCA PDF (summary + timelines) and an initial stability playbook draft that consolidates corrective actions across latency, throughput, and elevated 5xx rates during the 2026-11-01 incident. This thread will be the canonical tracking thread for action owners and exec readouts.

Key highlights in the RCA (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a combination of a model shard imbalance introduced during rollout + an aggressive autoscaling window that delayed additional capacity by ~75s under the traffic surge.
- Customer impact: average p95 latency spiked from 360ms to 3.1s; sustained 5xx rate peaked at 4.8% for 22 minutes; throughput dropped ~28% on critical endpoints.
- Short-term mitigations already applied: roll back to model-v12.1; raised autoscaling aggressiveness; applied KV-cache retention tweak to reduce cold-start penalties.

Immediate asks / next steps: 
1) Review the attached stability-playbook-v1.md and confirm owners for each play (we included suggested owners in the guide).
2) Kimberly: finalize the dedicated capacity burst schedule and confirm cost & quota implications.
3) Marcus: validate the kernel-level fallback patch; target staging test by EOD Thu.
4) Neha: prepare a one-page exec summary for Aurora execs and a proposed weekly cadence (30-min) until SLA metrics are stable for two consecutive weeks.

I will host a follow-up readout Friday 11/06 10:00 PT to walk Aurora leadership through the playbook and ownership ladder unless you request sooner.

Attachments: aurora-rca-20261103.pdf, stability-playbook-v1.md, ownership-ladder.csv

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

+1 on the framing — good work on the RCA. A couple of quick clarifications from the customer side that I want to capture before the Friday readout: 
- Aurora asked for a short-term SLA credit proposal if we miss p95 again during the next 30 days. Jenna: can you confirm whether that will be required or if Aurora prefers an enhanced monitoring + playbook instead?
- On the playbook, we should add an "emergency bypass" flow to route critical customers to warm pinned nodes when autoscale lags; that reduces customer-visible latency while capacity stabilizes.

Action items assigned to me: I will draft the exec one-pager and include three scenarios (best, expected, worst) and the proposed SLA credit language for legal review. Target: Thu 11/05 12:00 PT.

Neha

Kimberly here — reviewing capacity options. Notes: 
- Dedicated burst: we can provide a 2-hour burst pool that adds 12 T4s for critical periods; cost estimate attached in the playbook appendix.
- Quota impact: need procurement sign-off if Aurora wants sustained bursts > 6 hrs/day.
- Short-term operational change: I'll add a checklist in the playbook for immediate manual burst triggers (SRE on-call + account CS rep).

I'll post a short-runbook and cost delta by Thu 11/05 EOD. If Aurora would prefer a standing reserved pool instead, let's flag that in Friday's readout as an option.

Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora stability debrief - initial RCA and next steps

Quick technical update: 
- I validated the kernel-fallback patch in internal staging. It prevents the shard imbalance from routing too many decoder steps to a single worker under the traffic distribution observed. Latency improvements in staging: median -12%, p95 -35% on synthetic replay matching Aurora's pattern.
- Risk: the fallback increases memory pressure by ~6% under heavy long-context workloads. I added a toggle to the runtime config so we can enable for Aurora only while we validate broader perf impact.

Planned timeline: staging validation complete by Thu 11/05 18:00 PT; can push to production canary 11/06 AM if all clear.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
